headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: dexter’s broad egress and API use can expose Botpress-generated content, while shared file/workflow assumptions are undocumented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Botpress has no documented shared channel or output ingestion surface, while dexter has autonomous execution and file/API surfaces that could be bridged by manual copy-paste or shared files. The pairwise injection path is not documented, so this is limited to unusual operator wiring rather than default hijack risk.
conditions: IF the operator copies Botpress outputs into dexter prompts or scratchpad files, injection becomes plausible.
IF both agents are connected through a shared filesystem or message queue, attacker-controlled text can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable any copy-paste bridge between Botpress and dexter.
Review dexter inputs for instruction-like text before execution.
Use a human approval step before dexter acts on Botpress output.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all cross-agent messages.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dexter explicitly touches financial and market data and has broad network egress plus multiple API calls, while Botpress is a customer-support agent with package-install capability and no egress restriction documented. If Botpress receives sensitive customer content and passes it to dexter, dexter can transmit it to third-party APIs by default, creating an exfiltration path.
conditions: IF Botpress is fed customer records, secrets, or regulated support tickets and forwards them to dexter, leakage occurs.
IF dexter runs with its documented API calls enabled, any forwarded content can leave the environment.
mitigations: Do not pass sensitive support data from Botpress to dexter.
Restrict dexter API keys to non-sensitive test data.
Redact customer identifiers before any handoff.
Run dexter in a separate tenant or network segment.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on Botpress-to-dexter transfers.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Botpress can install packages, and dexter supports multiple instances plus autonomous execution with file and API surfaces. The profiles do not prove a shared writable directory, but if they are co-located the overlapping mutation and execution behaviors can conflict on shared resources or dependencies.
conditions: IF both agents share the same filesystem or dependency environment, package changes can interfere.
IF dexter instances run concurrently against the same scratchpad, writes can race.
mitigations: Pin dependencies for Botpress.
Give dexter a unique scratchpad per run.
Avoid running package installs during dexter jobs.
Serialize writes to any shared directory.
requires-engineering: add file locks around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dexter’s autonomous execution and API/tool surfaces make it likely to act on upstream text, while Botpress is a support agent that can generate user-facing content. The profiles do not show verification between them, so Botpress output could become dexter input with no check, causing incorrect downstream actions or reports.
conditions: IF dexter consumes Botpress responses as task instructions, errors can propagate.
IF Botpress outputs are used as facts without validation, dexter may act on false premises.
mitigations: Require a verification step before dexter acts.
Limit Botpress output to structured fields.
Have a human review high-impact dexter actions.
Log source provenance for every dexter input.
requires-engineering: add schema validation between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Dexter touches financial and market data and uses multiple external APIs, while Botpress is a customer-support agent that may handle customer data. The profiles do not specify residency or retention controls, so a compliance mismatch is plausible if support data is forwarded into dexter’s third-party services.
conditions: IF Botpress processes customer support data that includes regulated personal data and forwards it to dexter APIs, policy mismatch can occur.
IF the deployment requires residency or retention guarantees, dexter’s external APIs may violate them.
mitigations: Classify data before any handoff.
Block regulated data from dexter API calls.
Review API vendor terms and retention settings.
Keep support and research workloads separate.
requires-engineering: implement residency-aware routing.
